Precautions Clindamycin should not be given to patients hypersen- sitive to it or to the closely related drug lincomycin. It should be used with caution in patients with a history of gastrointestinal disease, particularly colitis, and stopped immediately if significant diarrhoea or colitis occurs. Middle-aged and elderly female patients may be at greater risk of severe diarrhoea or pseudomem- branous colitis. Caution has also been advised in atopic patients. Periodic tests of liver and kidney function and blood counts have been recommended in patients re- ceiving prolonged therapy, and in infants. Caution is required during parenteral use in neonates, since some parenteral formulations contain benzyl alcohol which may cause fatal ‘gasping syndrome’ (see p.1632). AIDS.
